run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network frontend gateway nginx-thrift is in CrashLoopBackOff because its only running pod was admitted with memory requests=limits=16Mi and is repeatedly OOMKilled (exit 137), taking the whole HTTP entry point down: the wrk2 load generator on the nginx-thrift Service IP 10.96.70.81:8080 logs 'Connection refused'. The 16Mi values are not in the nginx-thrift Deployment/ReplicaSet template (256Mi limit / 128Mi request); they match exactly the patch emitted by the mutating admission webhook served by Deployment platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops, whose ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server sets requests.memory and limits.memory to MEMORY="16Mi", and which is registered through five MutatingWebhookConfigurations (cert-manager-webhook, gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, istio-sidecar-injector, kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config) scoped to namespace social-network. Only the one pod created after those webhook registrations (12:28:40Z) carries 16Mi; the other 26 social-network pods predate them, have no memory limits and are ready. Downstream services were still serving HTTP 200 traces until the crash and show no error spans of their own.

claims.text: All 27 pods in namespace social-network were Running at the cluster read; the only pod not ready was nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh (ready=[false], restarts=[1]); the other 26 pods reported ready=[true] with restartCount 0.

Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh (ns social-network) has container nginx-thrift with resources requests.memory=16Mi and limits.memory=16Mi; its previous container instance terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-21T12:28:54Z, and the container was waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 10s restarting failed container=nginx-thrift').

The OOM kills continued: at the 12:30:26Z read the container's restartCount was 3, lastState.terminated.reason=OOMKilled with exitCode 137 and finishedAt 2026-11-21T12:29:44Z, and state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff with message 'back-off 40s restarting failed container=nginx-thrift'.

The Deployment nginx-thrift pod template declares limits.memory=256Mi and requests.memory=128Mi, and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 (created 2026-11-21T12:28:36Z, replicas 1) carries the same 256Mi/128Mi template, so the 16Mi values observed on pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh are not in the workload definition.

ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in namespace platform-ops contains server.py with MEMORY = "16Mi" and build_patch(), which emits JSONPatch ops setting /spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory and /spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory to MEMORY on the AdmissionReview object.

Deployment platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops (created 2026-11-21T12:28:38Z, 1/1 ready, availableReplicas 1) runs command [python /app/server.py] with ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server mounted at /app and a TLS secret at /certs.

Five MutatingWebhookConfigurations exist, all created 2026-11-21T12:28:40Z, all pointing at clientConfig.service platform-policy-controller / namespace platform-ops / path /mutate / port 443 with namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network and failurePolicy Fail: cert-manager-webhook (webhook.cert-manager.io), gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration (mutation.gatekeeper.sh, rules pods CREATE, no objectSelector), istio-sidecar-injector (rev.namespace.sidecar-injector.istio.io), kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg (mutate.kyverno.svc) and linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config (linkerd-proxy-injector.linkerd.io).

Only the pod created after those webhook registrations carries 16Mi: nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh (creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T12:28:48Z, limits.memory=16Mi, OOMKilled); the other 26 social-network pods were created 12:28:26Z-12:28:30Z, have no memory limits ('none') and are running.

The 16Mi memory requests/limits that killed the nginx-thrift container were applied at pod admission by the mutating webhook served by Deployment platform-policy-controller (namespace platform-ops): the pod was created 8s after the five webhook configurations were registered, its 16Mi requests=limits match the exact values build_patch() writes, and no other object or setting in the observed cluster produces that value for this pod.

nginx-thrift rollout timeline: ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 was scaled 0->1 at 12:28:36Z and old ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df scaled 1->0 at 12:28:38Z; pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-hh68g was created at 12:28:36Z and killed by kubelet ('Stopping container nginx-thrift') at 12:28:48Z, the same second ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 created replacement pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh.

Frontend connectivity failed: pod wrk2-job-946kh (container wrk2) logged 'unable to connect to 10.96.70.81:8080 Connection refused' at 2026-11-21T12:28:59Z plus 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 1066, write 13951, timeout 6' at 12:28:57Z, and Service nginx-thrift in namespace social-network has clusterIP 10.96.70.81, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080.

Until the crash the frontend was serving normally: nginx-web-server spans for /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read carry http.status_code=200 between 12:28:41.396Z and 12:28:45.695Z, and all 36 shown (service, operation) groups report error_rows=0, including compose-post-service, text-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, media-service, unique-id-service and user-service.

Deployment resources across namespace social-network: only nginx-thrift declares memory (limits 256Mi / requests 128Mi); the other 26 Deployments declare no memory limits or requests, which is why they still run unbounded while only the nginx-thrift pod created after the webhooks was forced to 16Mi.

No other social-network service shows its own failure: compose-post-service-659bfc5898-zxdck logged only 'Starting the compose-post-service server ...' at 12:28:30Z with no error lines, the other 26 pods are ready with restartCount 0, and the sampled traces of the downstream services contained no error rows, so they are not placed as affected.

Background noise not tied to this cause: mongodb index-creation errors at startup ('Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found ... user-mongodb:27017', 'social-graph-mongodb:27017', 'post-storage-mongodb:27017', 'url-shorten-mongodb:27017', 'user-timeline-mongodb:27017') were logged by user-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, url-shorten-service and user-timeline-service at 12:28:27Z-12:28:31Z, before the frontend crash, and those services later produced only successful spans. The only Warning events in the window (a type=Warning listing at 12:30:50Z) are in namespace observe: Pod loki-0 'Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503' at 12:27:56Z and StatefulSet loki FailedUpdate on PVC storage-loki-0 at 12:27:19Z.

A namespaced LimitRange defaulting memory to 16Mi was considered as the source of the 16Mi; it is rejected because the ReplicaSet template already specified limits.memory=256Mi and requests.memory=128Mi, and a LimitRange default only fills fields a container omits (it cannot lower an explicit limit), while the observed pod value matches the webhook's patch value exactly.

Because the five webhook configurations are still registered and still target every pod CREATE in namespace social-network, any newly created pod there (rollout, restart, reschedule) will also be forced to 16Mi and is likely to be OOM-killed the same way; this is unverified because no second social-network workload has been created since the webhooks were registered.

Remove or repair the fault-injecting admission path (delete the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations that point to platform-policy-controller.platform-ops/mutate and remove Deployment/ConfigMap platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops), then delete pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh so it is recreated from the 256Mi/128Mi template and confirm its resources and readiness.

gaps: LimitRange objects cannot be read with the available Kubernetes tools (kind limitranges is refused with INVALID_PARAMS), so a namespace-level default limit is argued away by mechanism (LimitRange cannot lower an explicit limit) rather than shown absent.

What deleted pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-hh68g at 2026-11-21T12:28:48Z is unknown: the only record is the kubelet 'Stopping container nginx-thrift' event; no API audit trail or change history source is integrated, and the deleter is not named in any retained object or event.

No AdmissionReview request/response is observable: the platform-policy-controller container writes no log lines (0 lines read) and audit logging is not available, so the mutation of pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qjjhh is inferred from the exact value, timing and code, not observed directly.

Prometheus returned no samples for traces_span_metrics_calls_total (get_series for 12:19Z-12:29Z was empty) and no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series at all, so no error-rate or latency reading and no before/after latency baseline exist for this incident.

kube-state-metrics has no series for namespace social-network: kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned 15 series, none for social-network, and kube_replicaset_owner{namespace="social-network",replicaset=~"nginx-thrift.*"} returned nothing; pod/deployment status therefore came only from the Kubernetes API at read time.

All social-network pods were created at 12:28:26Z-12:28:30Z, so nothing before 12:28:26Z is observable; traces stop at 12:28:45Z (Jaeger memory storage) and the pre-rollout pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-cjdct's logs are no longer retrievable.
The webhook TLS secret referenced by Deployment platform-policy-controller is redacted and was not read, so the certificate/CA configuration of the webhook could not be verified.

An earlier event grouping at 12:29:05Z showed one type=Warning reason=BackOff event on a Pod in namespace social-network; a later type=Warning listing at 12:30:50Z returned only two observe-namespace events (and reported 1 event dropped as outside the window), so the exact Warning-event set is not fully reconstructable.
next_steps: Have a human confirm with cluster audit logs or the platform-ops change history who deleted pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-hh68g and when the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations were installed.

Review all other admission webhooks/namespaces for the same platform-policy-controller backend before further rollouts, since the registrations masquerade as cert-manager, gatekeeper, istio, kyverno and linkerd.

After removing the webhook, watch the next pod created in social-network to confirm it keeps the Deployment's 128Mi/256Mi values and stays ready, and confirm wrk2 traffic to 10.96.70.81:8080 stops returning connection refused.

import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return

httpd = HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8443), Handler)
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain("/certs/tls.crt", "/certs/tls.key")
httpd.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(httpd.socket, server_side=True)
httpd.serve_forever()
